benchmarks.title: Equidistant Poles & Equilateral Triangle
benchmarks.geometric_essence: From two distinct seed points A and B, construct the two congruent circles (A, B) and (B, A) and select their intersection poles F and E to form equilateral triangle ABF. Tests whether a system can actually prove circle-circle intersection existence and select one of the two quadratic roots.

leaneuclid.code:
theorem proposition_1 : ∀ (a b : Point) (AB : Line),
    distinctPointsOnLine a b AB →
    ∃ c : Point, |(a─c)| = |(a─b)| ∧ |(b─c)| = |(b─a)| ∧ ¬(c.onLine AB) := by
  euclid_intros
  euclid_apply (Circles.from_points a b) as α
  euclid_apply (Circles.from_points b a) as β
  euclid_apply (Intersections.intersect_circles α β) as c
  use c
  euclid_finish
leaneuclid.reveals: Explicitly justifies why circles α and β must intersect via System E's diagrammatic circle-intersection axiom (filling Euclid's famous Book I.1 gap). Prop01.lean also proves proposition_1' selecting the pole on a chosen side via intersect_circles_same_side!
leaneuclid.hides: Delegates all interior/exterior circle-containment verification to external Z3/CVC5 via SMT_VERIF, and yields no coordinates for c.

geocoq.code:
Theorem proposition_01 :
  forall A B, neq A B -> exists X, equilateral A B X /\ Triangle A B X.
Proof.
  intros.
  pose proof (postulate_Euclid3 A B H) as [J HJ].
  pose proof (postulate_Euclid3 B A (neq_sym _ _ H)) as [K HK].
  ... (* applies postulate_circle_circle to obtain witness C *)
geocoq.reveals: Isolates the exact continuity axiom (circle_circle, equivalent over Tarski neutral geometry to nested-circle continuity) required for I.1 to hold over Euclidean fields rather than Q^2.
geocoq.hides: In pure Tarski point-only files, circles do not exist as objects—circle_circle is stated as a 6-point existential sentence on Bet and Cong.

mathlib4.code:
-- NO constructive Euclid I.1 existence theorem in Mathlib/Geometry/Euclidean/!
-- Equilateral triangles appear only hypothetically as dist-equality assumptions:
variable {V P : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V]
  [MetricSpace P] [NormedAddTorsor V P]
-- Hypothesis form: dist a b = r ∧ dist b c = r ∧ dist c a = r
mathlib4.reveals: Shows sharply that mathlib4 is an analytic deductive library over arbitrary dimension n (where two spheres in R^3 meet in a circle, not 2 points!), not a planar constructive system.
mathlib4.hides: Cannot construct the two planar apexes without choosing an explicit 2D Orientation and invoking Orientation.rotation (π / 3).

alphageometry.code:
# Primitive two-circle locus intersection + Pons Asinorum (r13):
a b = segment a b; c = on_circle c a b, on_circle c b a ? eqangle a b a c b c b a

# Or macro stanza in defs.txt:37-41:
eq_triangle x a b
x : a b
a b = diff a b
x : cong x a a b, cong x b a b; eqangle a b a x b x b a
alphageometry.reveals: Compact 1-line locus intersection syntax; also exposes the silent ';' drop quirk in defs.txt:40 where the post-semicolon eqangle is ignored by Graph.add_clause and re-proved by r13.
alphageometry.hides: Cannot prove absolute angle π/3 (aconst a b a c 1 3) from circle intersections alone because AngleTable works modulo π without triangle interior-sum orientation!

newclid.code: a b = segment a b; c = on_circle c a b, on_circle c b a ? cong c a c b; eqangle a b a c b c b a
newclid.reveals: Multi-goal ';' syntax after '?' verifies both side congruence and base-angle equality in a single run.
newclid.hides: Which of the two poles c lands on depends on random float64 sampling inside the numerical sketcher.

jgex.reveals: Expresses the 60-degree cosine relation purely rationally via Pythagoras difference P_CAB / P_ABA = 1/2.
jgex.hides: Root branch selection between upper and lower equilateral apexes.

pga_cga.code:
q_AB = -2 * (A | B)                        # exact quadrance |A - B|^2
kA = A - sp.Rational(1, 2) * q_AB * ni     # dual circle centered at A through B
kB = B - sp.Rational(1, 2) * q_AB * ni     # dual circle centered at B through A
T = (kA ^ kB).dual()                       # OPNS grade-2 point pair F ^ E
s = sp.sqrt((T * T).e)                     # invariant scalar separation
F = norm_pt((T + s) * (T | ni))            # upper pole via projector split
E = norm_pt((T - s) * (T | ni))            # lower pole via projector split
pga_cga.reveals: The circle-circle intersection is a single algebraic object—the grade-2 bivector point pair T = F ^ E—before splitting its two roots via idempotent projectors (T ± s)!
pga_cga.hides: Requires lifting 2D plane into 4D Minkowski space R^{3,1} (since 2D PGA lacks circle blades).

cindyjs.reveals: Maintains continuous identity of poles F and E under arbitrary dragging via Riemann-surface homotopy continuation.
cindyjs.hides: Coordinates are complex floats (F = [1, 1.7320508..., 1]); requires PSLQ guess() to recover sqrt(3).

sympy_geometry.code:
r = A.distance(B)
E, F = Circle(A, r).intersection(Circle(B, r))  # invokes generic CAS solve()!
sympy_geometry.reveals: Concise object-oriented syntax returning two exact symbolic Point2D instances over Q(sqrt(3)).
sympy_geometry.hides: Calls generic Buchberger/CAS solve() under the hood (stalling on nested steps) and returns roots sorted arbitrarily without a half-plane selector.

byrne_1847.source_ref: Byrne (1847) Book I, Prop. 1 / Rougeux c82.net/euclid/book1#prop1
byrne_1847.code:
Given:        [black ━━]                       (seed segment)
To Construct: △([black ━━], [red ━━], [yellow ━━]) equilateral
Construction: Describe [red ○] about left end with radius [black ━━]   (Post. 3)
              Describe [blue ○] about right end with radius [black ━━] (Post. 3)
              From intersection draw [red ━━] and [yellow ━━]          (Post. 1)
Proof:        [red ━━]    = [black ━━]   (radii of [red ○], Def. 15)
              [yellow ━━] = [black ━━]   (radii of [blue ○], Def. 15)
            ∴ [red ━━] = [yellow ━━] = [black ━━]                      (Ax. 1)
byrne_1847.reveals: Zero vertex letters! Every segment and circle is a direct coloured value-token whose equality follows visually from shared circle-radius membership.
byrne_1847.hides: Like classical Euclid, assumes visually that [red ○] and [blue ○] intersect without an explicit continuity axiom, and addresses the apex only as 'their intersection'.

geometor_model.code:
m = Model("equidistant_poles", auto_intersect=False)
a = m.set_point(0, 0, ID="A"); b = m.set_point(2, 0, ID="B")
c_a = m.construct_circle(a, b, ID="( A B )")
c_b = m.construct_circle(b, a, ID="( B A )")
f = m.intersect(c_a, c_b, side_of=(a, b, +1), ID="F")  # exact (1, sqrt(3))
e = m.intersect(c_a, c_b, side_of=(a, b, -1), ID="E")  # exact (1, -sqrt(3))
m.assert_equal((a, b), (a, f), (b, f), by="I.1")       # Q = 4, spread = 3/4
geometor_model.reveals: Combines closed-form radical-axis algebra (zero solve()), System E half-plane root selection side_of=(a, b, ±1), exact Q(sqrt(3)) coordinates, and rational spread verification s = 3/4.
geometor_model.hides: Currently 2D planar; selector AST should be persisted on Step for direct LeanEuclid export.

benchmarks.title: Perpendicular Bisector & Midpoint
benchmarks.geometric_essence: Join the two equidistant vesica poles F and E of (A, B) and (B, A) to obtain the perpendicular bisector [E F] and intersect with [A B] to obtain the midpoint M. Contrasts synthetic kite/congruence proofs against 1-subtraction conformal duals.

leaneuclid.code:
theorem proposition_10 : ∀ (a b : Point) (AB : Line),
    distinctPointsOnLine a b AB → ∃ d : Point, between a d b ∧ |(a─d)| = |(d─b)| := by
  euclid_intros
  euclid_apply (proposition_1' a b AB) as c
  euclid_apply (Prop09.proposition_9' b a c ...) as CD
  euclid_apply (Intersections.intersect_lines AB CD) as d
  euclid_apply (Prop04.proposition_4 c a d c b d)  -- SAS congruence
  euclid_finish
leaneuclid.reveals: Follows Euclid's exact deductive chain (equilateral apex -> angle bisector I.9 -> Pasch line intersection -> SAS I.4) and proves d lies strictly between a and b!
leaneuclid.hides: Uses Euclid's 2-triangle angle-bisector construction rather than Lemoine's more economical 2-pole vesica chord [E F].

geocoq.code:
Lemma midpoint_existence : forall A B, exists X, Midpoint X A B.
(* Proven in neutral geometry WITHOUT circle-circle continuity via Gupta's
   clever perpendicular-projection construction! *)
geocoq.reveals: Astonishing metatheoretic insight: unlike Euclid I.10 (which uses I.1 and thus circle-circle continuity), midpoint existence holds in pure Hilbert/Tarski neutral geometry over smaller Pythagorean fields!
geocoq.hides: Requires ~150 lines of intricate Tarski point-only lemmas in Ch08.

mathlib4.code:
def perpBisector (p₁ p₂ : P) : AffineSubspace ℝ P :=
  mk' (midpoint ℝ p₁ p₂) (ℝ ∙ (p₁ -ᵥ p₂))ᗮ

theorem mem_perpBisector_iff_dist_eq (p p₁ p₂ : P) :
    p ∈ perpBisector p₁ p₂ ↔ dist p p₁ = dist p p₂
mathlib4.reveals: Defines the perpendicular bisector hyperplane in arbitrary dimension n as the orthogonal complement (p₁ -ᵥ p₂)ᗮ through midpoint ℝ p₁ p₂, and proves the equidistance locus iff in 8 lines.
mathlib4.hides: Assumes 1/2 scalar division in ℝ up front (midpoint := lineMap p₁ p₂ (1/2)) rather than constructing it with a compass.

alphageometry.code: a b = segment a b; c = on_circle c a b, on_circle c b a; d = on_circle d a b, on_circle d b a; m = on_line m a b, on_line m c d ? midp m a b
alphageometry.reveals: Demonstrates AlphaGeometry's clever HoleCircle mechanism: once c is sampled at one lens pole, repeating the exact same clause for d automatically punctures c and selects the opposite pole d != c!
alphageometry.hides: Relies on kite rule r23 + reflected congruence r37 rather than explicit half-plane opposition.

newclid.code: a b = segment a b; m = on_line m a b, on_bline m a b ? midp m a b; rconst m a a b 1/2
newclid.reveals: Explicitly links perpendicular-bisector intersection (on_bline) to midpoint (R54) and sound constant ratio 1/2 (R51).
newclid.hides: Treats on_bline as a primitive 1-step locus rather than unfolding the two congruent circles.

jgex.reveals: 4-point Pythagoras difference P_ACBD proves kite diagonal orthogonality in 1 subtraction without square roots!
jgex.hides: Symmetric opposite-side orientation S_CBD = S_ACD must be supplied for the two circle roots.

pga_cga.source_ref: 2D PGA Cl(2,0,1) & 2D CGA Cl(3,1) in kingdon
pga_cga.code:
# 2D PGA (division-free & radical-free!):
l_bis_pga = (A & B) | (A + B)
M_pga = sp.Rational(1, 2) * (A + B)

# 2D CGA (perpendicular bisector is literally A - B!):
l_bis_dual = A - B   # -2*((A - B) | X) = |X - A|^2 - |X - B|^2 == 0!
M_cga = sp.Rational(1, 2) * (A + B) + sp.Rational(1, 4) * (A | B) * ni
pga_cga.reveals: In 2D CGA, subtracting two unit null points A - B IS the dual perpendicular bisector hyperplane because their quadratic terms cancel to the equidistance locus!
pga_cga.hides: Bypasses the vesica circle construction entirely.

cindyjs.code:
M = B_3 * A + A_3 * B;               // homogeneous midpoint [xA+xB, yA+yB, 2]
l_AB = cross(A, B);                  // join(A, B)
l_bis = cross(fundDual * l_AB, M);   // CindyScript: perp(join(A, B), midpoint(A, B))
cindyjs.reveals: Shows Cayley-Klein orthogonality in action: multiplying line l_AB by fundDual = diag(1,1,0) produces its orthogonal ideal point [a, b, 0], which is crossed with M.
cindyjs.hides: Division-free affine shortcut rather than compass construction.

sympy_geometry.code:
seg = Segment(A, B)
M = seg.midpoint
l_bis = seg.perpendicular_bisector()
sympy_geometry.reveals: Clean 2-line high-level API returning exact rational Point2D and Line2D whenever A, B are rational.
sympy_geometry.hides: Triggers eager simplify() calls inside midpoint and Line coefficients.

byrne_1847.source_ref: Byrne (1847) Book I, Props. 10 & 11 / Rougeux c82.net/euclid/book1#prop10
byrne_1847.code:
Given:        [black ━━] = [yellow ━━] + [blue ━━]
Construction: Construct equilateral △([red ━━], [red ━━], [black ━━])  (I.1)
              Bisect apex wedge into [yellow ◣] = [red ◣] by [black ╌╌╌] (I.9)
Proof:        [red ━━] = [red ━━],  [black ╌╌╌] common,  [yellow ◣] = [red ◣]
            ∴ [yellow ━━] = [blue ━━]                                  (I.4)
byrne_1847.reveals: Stroke grammar in action: solid strokes mark Given/target halves while dashed [black ╌╌╌] marks the auxiliary angle-bisector cut.
byrne_1847.hides: Follows Euclid's I.1 -> I.9 -> I.4 triangle chain rather than the direct 2-pole vesica chord [E F].

geometor_model.code:
with m.subconstruction("bisect_AB") as scope:
    c1 = m.construct_circle(a, b, guide=True); c2 = m.construct_circle(b, a, guide=True)
    f = m.intersect(c1, c2, side_of=(a, b, +1), guide=True)
    e = m.intersect(c1, c2, side_of=(a, b, -1), guide=True)
    bis = m.construct_line(e, f, ID="[ E F ]")
    mid = m.intersect(l_ab, bis, between=(a, b), ID="M")
    scope.keep(mid, bis)
geometor_model.reveals: Unfolds the genuine compass-and-straightedge vesica construction, cancels √3 identically when [E F] meets [A B] so M stays purely in Q(A, B), and folds auxiliary circles neatly via subconstruction!
geometor_model.hides: Re-running 2 circles per midpoint adds construction steps unless cached as a reusable macro.

benchmarks.title: Parallel Line Through an External Point
benchmarks.geometric_essence: Construct the unique Euclidean line through external point P parallel to line AB. Exposes how each system treats the Parallel Postulate, points at infinity, alternate interior angles, or rhombus symmetry.

leaneuclid.code:
theorem proposition_31 : ∀ (a b c : Point) (BC : Line),
    distinctPointsOnLine b c BC ∧ ¬(a.onLine BC) →
    ∃ EF : Line, a.onLine EF ∧ ¬(EF.intersectsLine BC) := by
  euclid_intros
  -- Picks d on BC, copies angle ∠(a:d:c) to vertex a via Prop23, applies Prop27:
  euclid_apply (Prop23.proposition_23_opposing ...) as e
  euclid_apply (Lines.from_points e a) as EF
  euclid_apply (Prop27.proposition_27 e a b c ...)
  euclid_finish
leaneuclid.reveals: Proves existence of a non-intersecting line in pure neutral geometry (Prop 27 alternate interior angles—Playfair uniqueness is not needed until Prop 29/30!).
leaneuclid.hides: Euclid's angle-copying construction (via I.23 -> I.22) has much higher Lemoine complexity than rhombus or double-perpendicular constructions.

geocoq.code:
Lemma parallel_existence : forall A B P, A <> B ->
  exists C, exists D, C <> D /\ Par A B C D /\ Col P C D.
(* Existence proven in neutral geometry via double midpoint reflection;
   uniqueness proved equivalent to 34 distinct parallel postulates! *)
geocoq.reveals: Cleanly separates neutral parallel existence (central reflection across a midpoint!) from the 34 equivalent parallel-uniqueness postulates cataloged in parallel_postulates.v.
geocoq.hides: Representing the output line requires two existential witness points C, D with C <> D and Col P C D.

mathlib4.reveals: In an affine torsor, a parallel subspace through p is tautologically mk' p s.direction—Playfair's postulate is baked directly into linear-algebraic coset structure!
mathlib4.hides: Cannot study non-Euclidean neutral geometry without abandoning AffineSpace.

alphageometry.code:
# Synthetic double-perpendicular construction (1 deduction step via r00):
a b c = triangle a b c; f = foot f c a b; d = on_tline d c c f ? para c d a b
alphageometry.reveals: Rule r00 (AB ⊥ CF ∧ CD ⊥ CF => AB || CD) gives an immediate 1-step synthetic proof.
alphageometry.hides: Conflates parallel existence and Playfair uniqueness (r28: para A B A C => coll A B C).

newclid.code: a = free a; b = free b; c = free c; d = on_tline d c a b; f = on_tline f c c d ? para a b c f
newclid.hides: Assumes Euclidean metric direction group ℝ/πℤ.

jgex.code:
POINT A B C; FOOT F C A B; ON_TLINE D C C F; SHOW: PARALLEL C D A B.
# Area goal: S_CABD = S_CAB - S_DAB = -(r/4) P_AFBC = 0 (since CF ⊥ AB => P_AFBC = 0)
jgex.reveals: Dualizes 90-degree rotation (TRATIO) directly between signed area S_CABD and Pythagoras difference P_AFBC!
jgex.hides: Requires choosing auxiliary ratio parameter r != 0 along the perpendicular.

pga_cga.code:
# Projective form: join P with the ideal point (L ^ e0) where L meets infinity!
L_para = P & (L ^ e0)
# Equivalent metric double-contraction (no explicit e0 needed):
L_para_metric = (L | P) | P
pga_cga.reveals: Reveals the projective essence of parallelism: a parallel line through P is simply the join (&) of P with L's ideal point at infinity (L ^ e0)!

cindyjs.code: L_para = cross(cross(linf, L), P);   // CindyScript: para(L, P)
cindyjs.reveals: Identical projective elegance in CP^2: cross(linf, L) is the ideal point of L on z=0, and crossing with P joins it to P in 6 multiplications.
cindyjs.hides: Euclidean vs hyperbolic parallelism depends on the chosen fundamental conic.

sympy_geometry.hides: Parallel lines have L.intersection(L_para) == [], losing the ideal point at infinity.

byrne_1847.source_ref: Byrne (1847) Book I, Prop. 31 / Rougeux c82.net/euclid/book1#prop31
byrne_1847.code:
Given:        Point • and line [black ━━]
Construction: Draw transversal [yellow ╌╌╌] from • to [black ━━]       (Post. 1)
              Copy alternate wedge [red ◣] = [blue ◣] via [red ━━]     (I.23)
Proof:        Alternate wedges [red ◣] = [blue ◣]
            ∴ [red ━━] ∥ [black ━━]                                    (I.27)
byrne_1847.reveals: Replaces Euclid's six vertex pointers (A, B, C, D, E, F) with two coloured angle wedges [red ◣] = [blue ◣], making the alternate-interior-angle mechanism instantaneous.
byrne_1847.hides: Notice Byrne MUST print a tiny black dot/star for the given external point because pure 0D points have no coloured line/region glyph!

geometor_model.code:
# Pure 3-circle compass rhombus (Lemoine-optimal) or double perpendicular:
q = m.intersect(l_ab, m.construct_circle(a, p, guide=True), on_ray=(a, b), guide=True)
d = m.intersect(m.construct_circle(p, a, guide=True), m.construct_circle(q, a, guide=True),
                side_of=(a, p, -1), ID="D")
l_para = m.construct_line(p, d, ID="[ P D ]")
m.assert_parallel(l_ab, l_para, by="I.31")  # exact line_spread == 0
geometor_model.reveals: Achieves parallel construction in just 3 congruent-radius circles (rhombus APDQ) and certifies exact parallelism via rational line_spread == 0.
geometor_model.hides: Could also expose a 1-line projective bridge cross(cross(linf, l_ab), p) in geometor.pappus.

benchmarks.title: Pythagorean Theorem & Right-Triangle Orthogonality
benchmarks.geometor_signature: pythagoras(A, B, C) -> Q(A, B) == Q(A, C) + Q(B, C)
benchmarks.geometric_essence: For right-angled triangle ABC (orthogonality at C), the quadrance on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the quadrances on the legs—and geometrically, the area of the hypotenuse square equals the sum of the two leg squares (Euclid's Bride's Chair). Exposes a stunning expressiveness cliff in AlphaGeometry!

leaneuclid.code:
theorem proposition_47 : ∀ (a b c d e f g h k : Point) (AB BC AC ... : Line),
    formTriangle a b c AB BC CA ∧ ∠(b:a:c) = ∟ ∧
    Square b c e d ... ∧ Square a b f g ... ∧ Square a c k h ... →
    (△(b:c:d) + △(c:e:d)) = (△(a:b:f) + △(b:g:f)) + (△(a:c:k) + △(c:h:k))
leaneuclid.reveals: Formalizes Euclid's authentic cut-and-paste area proof (Bride's Chair) AND explicitly isolates 6 '-- Missed by Euclid' topological lemmas (Prop47.lean:25-60) proving the outward squares don't fold across the triangle!
leaneuclid.hides: Verbose 9-point, 10-line theorem signature because Square is an unbundled 12-argument relational macro.

geocoq.code:
Lemma pythagoras :
  forall O E E' A B C AC BC AB AC2 BC2 AB2,
  ~ Col O E E' -> Per A C B ->
  Length O E E' A C AC -> Length O E E' B C BC -> Length O E E' A B AB ->
  Prod O E E' AC AC AC2 -> Prod O E E' BC BC BC2 ->
  Sum O E E' AC2 BC2 AB2 -> Prod O E E' AB AB AB2.
geocoq.reveals: Proves a^2 + b^2 = c^2 purely synthetically inside Tarski's internal geometric segment field (Sum and Prod constructed on line OE with unit E via Pappus/Thales) with zero real numbers!
geocoq.hides: Requires carrying coordinate-line frame witnesses (O, E, E') through every arithmetic relation.

mathlib4.code:
theorem dist_sq_eq_dist_sq_add_dist_sq_iff_angle_eq_pi_div_two (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) :
    dist p₁ p₃ * dist p₁ p₃ = dist p₁ p₂ * dist p₁ p₂ + dist p₃ p₂ * dist p₃ p₂ ↔
      ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π / 2 ∨ p₁ = p₂ ∨ p₃ = p₂
mathlib4.reveals: Immediate consequence of ‖u - v‖^2 = ‖u‖^2 + ‖v‖^2 - 2⟪u, v⟫ in any Hilbert/inner-product space of arbitrary dimension n, including degenerate endpoint disjuncts!
mathlib4.hides: Reduces Euclid's deep geometric theorem to a 3-line inner-product expansion, hiding the constructive equivalence of geometric squares.

alphageometry.source_ref: Expressiveness Ceiling! (ar.py lacks squared lengths; uses eqratio / contri)
alphageometry.code:
# CANNOT state AB^2 + AC^2 = BC^2! Must reformulate multiplicatively as AB^2 = BH * BC:
a b c = r_triangle a b c; h = foot h a b c ? eqratio b a b c b h b a
# Or prove Bride's Chair triangle congruence ΔABD ≅ ΔFBC:
a b c = r_triangle a b c; f g = square b a f g; d e = square b c d e ? contri a b d f b c
alphageometry.reveals: Major architectural revelation: AlphaGeometry's RatioTable (log-lengths) and DistanceTable (collinear 1st-power lengths) CANNOT express a^2 + b^2 = c^2!
alphageometry.hides: Any theorem requiring additive quadratic relations (Stewart, Apollonius median, disjoint radical axis) hits a hard wall in pure AlphaGeometry.

newclid.code:
# C++ Yuclid additive squared-length AR table + Newclid lequation rule R85:
a b = segment a b; c = free c; d = on_tline d c a b ? lequation 1/1 a c * a c 1/1 b d * b d -1/1 a d * a d -1/1 b c * b c 0
newclid.reveals: Shows exactly how Newclid/Yuclid broke past AlphaGeometry's ceiling by adding a dedicated additive squared-length Gaussian elimination table!
newclid.hides: In Newclid's Python engine, lequation is not yet wired into SympyARDeductor (only active in C++ Yuclid).

jgex.code:
# In the Area Method, Pythagoras is a 0-step DEFINITIONAL identity:
# P_ACB := AC^2 + CB^2 - AB^2, and PERPENDICULAR(C,A, C,B) <=> P_ACB = 0!
SHOW: (AREA A B F G) + (AREA A C K H) = (AREA B C E D).  # 4-line TRATIO proof!
jgex.reveals: By choosing P_ACB = AC^2 + CB^2 - AB^2 as a primitive coordinate-free invariant, Chou-Gao-Zhang make Pythagoras literally 0 = 0, AND ship 20 visual dissection proofs in 4_PYTH/!
jgex.hides: Area.java GUI tab is disabled in the Java port.

pga_cga.source_ref: 2D PGA Cl(2,0,1) & 2D CGA Cl(3,1) in kingdon
pga_cga.code:
# 2D PGA: squared norm of join line (A & B) IS Euclidean quadrance!
la, lb, lc = B & C, C & A, A & B
assert (la | lb).e == 0                                  # orthogonality
assert sp.expand((lc | lc).e - (la | la).e - (lb | lb).e) == 0

# 2D CGA: null inner product -2*(A | B) IS quadrance!
assert ((C ^ A ^ ni) | (C ^ B ^ ni)).e == 0
pga_cga.reveals: Both PGA line norms (l | l) and CGA null-point contractions -2*(A | B) natively compute Wildberger quadrances without a single square root.
pga_cga.hides: Algebraic expansion rather than geometric square dissection.
